issues.legal_issue: A tenant sublets premises when the premises were let to the tenant individually and another business takes exclusive possession, leaving the tenant without a right to possess them.
material_facts: The shop was let to the tenant individually, not to the joint family.
The tenant's business was later taken over by a partnership formed by his father and brothers.
The partnership exclusively occupied the shop, and the tenant was no longer its proprietor or entitled to possession there.
The rent authorities and the High Court found that the tenant had sublet the shop.
issues.conclusion: The concurrent finding that the tenant had sublet the shop was supported by the evidence and was unassailable.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(2)(ii)(a) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949 provides for eviction where a tenant sublets the premises without the landlord's written consent. The Court distinguished Hira Singh v. Banarsi Dass, which concerned joint tenants and held that one co-tenant's absence did not, by itself, establish subletting to the others.

rule.if: rent_eviction_proceeding and premises_let_to_individual_tenant and business_taken_over_by_another_business and other_business_has_exclusive_occupation and tenant_lacks_right_to_possession

predicates.rent_eviction_proceeding: A landlord pursued eviction on the ground that the tenant had sublet the premises.
predicates.premises_let_to_individual_tenant: The premises were let to one tenant individually rather than to the family or business later occupying them.
predicates.business_taken_over_by_another_business: A different business took over the business previously carried on by the tenant in the premises.
predicates.other_business_has_exclusive_occupation: The business that took over occupied the premises exclusively.
predicates.tenant_lacks_right_to_possession: The original tenant no longer had a right to possess the premises.

issues.definition: When eviction is pursued for subletting and the premises were let to an individual who later loses possession to a business that exclusively occupies them, the rule treats subletting as established.

issues.legal_issue: A subletting completed before a law's commencement cannot support eviction merely because the sublease continues afterward, but it can support eviction if a valid retrospective extension makes the law operative before the subletting occurred.
material_facts: The subletting was found to have occurred in 1967.
The rent-control law was first extended to the cantonment prospectively in 1969.
A later notification extended the law retrospectively, with the result that the law was deemed to have commenced there in 1950.
The sublease continued after the law became operative.
issues.conclusion: Because the valid retrospective extension made the law operative before the 1967 subletting, the landlord could rely on the statutory ground of subletting.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(2)(ii)(a) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949 refers to a subletting transaction completed after commencement; subletting is located at the point when the transaction is completed, rather than being a continuing transaction. Although the words “has sub-let” imply that an earlier sublease must subsist when the law commences, the clause's express reference to acts after commencement excludes a transaction completed before commencement. Goppulal v. Thakurji Shriji Shriji Dwarkadheeshji was distinguished because the provision considered there did not contain the same commencement limitation. The amended Cantonments (Extension of Rent Control Laws) Act, 1957 authorized retrospective extension, and the later notification made the rent law operative from a date before the subletting.

predicates.rent_eviction_proceeding: A landlord pursued eviction on the ground that the tenant had sublet the premises.
predicates.subletting_is_a_completed_transaction: The tenant completed the act transferring possession by subletting at a definite point in time.
predicates.retrospective_extension_validly_makes_la: A valid retrospective extension made the rent-control law operative before the tenant completed the subletting.

issues.definition: In an eviction proceeding based on subletting, a completed subletting supports the ground when a valid retrospective extension made the relevant law operative before that transaction occurred.

issues.legal_issue: A later extension notification is not an impermissible repeat of an exhausted power when an intervening statutory amendment creates a materially distinct power allowing retrospective extension.
material_facts: The government had issued an earlier notification extending the rent-control law prospectively.
A statutory amendment later authorized extensions from earlier or future dates, subject to stated limits.
After the amendment, the government issued a new notification extending the law retrospectively and superseding the earlier notification.
issues.conclusion: The later notification was issued under a separate and distinct power and was not invalid merely because the earlier power had already been exercised.
issues.legal_principle: The material components of a statutory power determine its character; powers with materially different components are distinct. The original power permitted prospective extension only, while the amended power permitted retrospective extension. Lachmi Narain v. Union of India was distinguishable because the power there had not materially changed between its first and later purported exercise.

predicates.challenge_to_later_extension_notificatio: A party challenged a later notification extending a law to a territory.
predicates.earlier_extension_power_was_exercised: The government had already used an earlier statutory power to extend the law to the territory.
predicates.intervening_amendment_created_materially: A statutory amendment introduced a materially different extension power before the later notification was issued.

issues.definition: A later extension notification is not invalid as an exhausted exercise when an earlier extension was made but an intervening amendment created a materially distinct power.

issues.legal_issue: The reference to “this Act” in a proviso added to a principal statute by amendment refers to the principal statute, not the amending statute.
material_facts: An amendment inserted a subsection and a proviso into the principal statute.
The proviso limited how far back an extension could take effect by reference to the commencement of “this Act.”
The principal statute was deemed to have commenced on an earlier date under the amended statutory scheme.
issues.conclusion: The words “this Act” referred to the principal statute, so the applicable commencement was that of the principal statute rather than the amending statute.
issues.legal_principle: The words “this Act” in clause (c) of the proviso to section 3(2) of the Cantonments (Extension of Rent Control Laws) Act, 1957 refer to the principal Act into which subsection (2) was inserted, not to the 1972 Amendment Act. Section 1(2), as amended, deemed the principal Act to have come into force on 26 January 1950.

predicates.interpretation_of_act_reference_in_amend: A court must determine what “this Act” refers to in a proviso introduced by an amendment.
predicates.proviso_is_inserted_into_principal_statu: The amendment inserted the proviso into an existing principal statute.

issues.definition: When a court interprets an act reference in a proviso inserted into a principal statute, the reference means the principal statute.
